audit_items.proof_trace: Direct INSERT by anon is blocked (REVOKE ALL in fix migration) and by authenticated is blocked (no INSERT RLS policy + FORCE RLS). However, `0001_create_attendance_schema.sql:9` grants ALL on functions in the attendance schema to authenticated via default privileges, meaning `record_attendance_by_card` — created later — is EXECUTE-accessible to authenticated; the fix migration only grants EXECUTE to anon explicitly and never revokes authenticated's EXECUTE. The SECURITY DEFINER function runs as postgres (bypasses RLS) and contains no `auth.uid()` ownership check (L22-50), so any authenticated caller can insert attendance rows for any valid card_id.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An authenticated user calls `supabase.rpc('record_attendance_by_card', { p_card_id: '<target_card_id>' })`; the SECURITY DEFINER function executes as postgres (bypassing all RLS), looks up the card_id owner, and inserts a forged attendance record into `attendance.attendances` — allowing any logged-in user to manipulate attendance history for themselves or any registered card whose ID they know.
